Overview

Injury Claims, Handled Personally

A personal injury claim is not just a form to fill out. It is a dispute with a company whose business model depends on paying you as little as possible.

The Price Law Firm handles the entire claim: preserving the evidence, identifying every party who may be responsible, documenting the full extent of your medical treatment and lost income, and pressing the insurer for a number that reflects what actually happened to you. If they will not get there, we file suit.

Below are the five kinds of cases we take. If you are not sure which describes yours — or whether you have a claim at all — call 850-215-2195. The consultation is free.

What a claim can cover

  • Emergency treatment, surgery, and ongoing medical care
  • Future medical costs where an injury is permanent
  • Wages lost while you were unable to work
  • Reduced ability to earn a living going forward
  • Pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life
  • Property damage from the collision

What is recoverable in any specific case depends on the facts, the injuries, and the insurance coverage available.

Case Types

Personal Injury Cases We Handle

Five focused practice areas. Click through for what each involves and how these claims are built.

Trucking Accidents

Commercial trucks are governed by federal safety rules, and more than one company may share the blame for a crash.

  • FMCSA-regulated carriers and driver hours-of-service rules
  • Catastrophic injury severity in truck-versus-car collisions
  • Multi-party liability: driver, carrier, loader, manufacturer
Learn More

Auto Accidents

Most injury claims start with an insurance adjuster whose job is to pay you as little as possible.

  • Dealing directly with insurance adjusters on your behalf
  • Florida's comparative negligence rule and shared fault
  • Whiplash, fractures, back injuries and long-term pain
Learn More

Catastrophic Injuries

When an injury changes the rest of your life, the claim has to account for the rest of your life.

  • Life-altering brain, spinal cord and burn injuries
  • Future medical care and lost earning capacity
  • Building the full long-term value of the claim
Learn More

Product Liability

A product that hurts you when used normally can make its manufacturer, distributor or retailer liable.

  • Design defects, manufacturing defects and failure to warn
  • Manufacturer, distributor and retailer responsibility
  • Recalled and dangerous consumer products
Learn More

Insurance Claims

A denial or a lowball offer is an opening position, not the final word on what your claim is worth.

  • Denied claims and bad-faith insurance practices
  • Lowball settlement offers and delayed payouts
  • Negotiating a fair number, or filing suit
Learn More

PFAS Contamination

Cancer and serious illness linked to "forever chemicals" in drinking water, firefighting foam and everyday products.

  • Kidney, testicular, liver, bladder and thyroid cancers
  • Contaminated tap water, AFFF firefighting foam, consumer goods
  • You do not need to have worked on a military base to qualify
Learn More

Also: Hurricane & Property Insurance Claims

Beyond injury work, the firm represents Panhandle homeowners and businesses whose hurricane and property damage claims have been denied, delayed or underpaid — an area where Bill Price has recovered $50 million in disputed coverage.

FAQ

Personal Injury FAQs

The consultation is free. Injury work is handled on a contingency fee — the attorney is paid out of any recovery rather than billing you month by month, and there is no fee unless we win.

The fee agreement is explained in full before you sign it.

For most negligence claims arising on or after March 24, 2023, Florida sets a two-year statute of limitations; before that date, a four-year period generally applied. Wrongful death claims run two years, and claims involving a government entity require written notice far sooner.

Deadlines turn on the specific facts and dates of your case, so please do not rely on a general rule. Call 850-215-2195 and we will confirm which deadline applies to you.

Get medical attention, even if you think you are fine — adrenaline masks injuries, and a delay in treatment gives the insurer an argument that you were not really hurt. Report the crash so there is an official record. Photograph everything: vehicle positions, damage, skid marks, road conditions, and your visible injuries. Collect witness names and numbers.

Then be careful. Do not give a recorded statement to the other side's insurer, and do not sign a medical authorization or a release before an attorney has looked at it.

Most do not. The large majority of injury claims resolve through settlement. But the settlements that reflect real value come from cases the other side believes are trial-ready, so we prepare every file that way. You decide whether to accept an offer — we give you our recommendation, and the call is yours.

It depends chiefly on your medical treatment. A claim should not be settled until your condition has stabilized enough to know what the long-term picture looks like — settling early can mean signing away the right to compensation for a problem that turns out to be permanent.

Straightforward claims can resolve in a few months. Serious injury cases, disputed liability, or cases that go into litigation take considerably longer. We will give you a realistic estimate once we have seen the file rather than a number designed to sound good.

You may still have a path to recovery. Florida drivers can carry uninsured/underinsured motorist (UM/UIM) coverage on their own policy, which is designed for exactly this situation, and there may be other applicable policies — a resident relative's coverage, an employer's policy if the at-fault driver was working, or a commercial policy.

Finding every available layer of coverage is part of the investigation. Read more on our insurance claims page.
